The writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been preferred seeking inter-alia a direction to the State respondent authorities to conduct a thorough investigation/inquiry by the Central Bureau of Investigation [CBI] or by any other competent investigation agency into the entire matter arising out of seizure of 2,780 bags of rice from the godown of the respondent no. 7 that was allegedly found unfit for human consumption by the Public Analyst, Assam and the consequent release of 545 nos. of bags of the seized rice for public consumption and the alleged destruction of only 1109 bags of the seized rice leaving 1126 nos. of bags of rice unaccounted by the authorities in the Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department, Assam.

sentences.text: It has been found averred in paragraph 1 of the writ petition that the association named 'Tinsukia Galla Kirana Committee' is representing the interests of 276 nos. of members engaged in trading of different essential commodities for public consumption.
The association is stated to be represented by its Secretary, who has been authorized by a resolution dated 30.05.2014 taken by the committee of the petitioner to institute the instant proceeding.
In paragraph 2 of the writ petition, it has been stated that the petition is being filed espousing issues that are of vital importance for the general public touching upon their health and safety.
The petitioner association has averred that its members belong to the trading community dealing in essential commodities.
5. It is an admitted position that the petitioner is an unregistered association.

6. In this connection, two decisions of the Division Bench of this Court in All Manipur DIC Supervisors' Association vs. State of Manipur and others , reported in 2000 [1] GLT 374 and Meghalaya Wine Dealers Association and another vs. State of Meghalaya and others , reported in 2010 [2] GLT 673 can be referred to.

entities.text: All Manipur DIC Supervisors' Association vs. State of Manipur and others , reported in 2000 [1] GLT 374
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Meghalaya Wine Dealers Association and another vs. State of Meghalaya and others , reported in 2010 [2] GLT 673
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In All Manipur DIC Supervisors Association [supra], the Division Bench has held that an unincorporated association has no legal personality and it is nothing but an aggregation of its members who can only bring legal proceedings in their individual capacity.

Even when all of them are affected by an official act, they can challenge that only if all the members join in the proceedings by name, the association, in such a case, cannot maintain an application under Article 226 or other legal proceeding in its own name.

In Meghalaya Wine Dealers Association [supra], it has been held that even when members form an association to protect their interest, as association it cannot file writ application as such association unless it attains the character of juristic person or a legal person by registering it under a statue.
When the association does not assume the character of a legal person it cannot enforce right in its favour.

It has, however,
been observed that individual Page No.# 4/4 members of such an association can file a writ application to assert his or her right when infringed.
But an unregistered association cannot have locus-standi to file a writ petition as it cannot be branded as an aggrieved person.

7. Having regard to the aforesaid position of law, as has been settled by the aforesaid two decisions of the Division Bench of this Court, this writ petition filed by an unregistered association is found to be not maintainable.
In such view of the matter, this writ petition is held to be not maintainable and therefore, the same is dismissed.
No cost.
